name: Ahjo
title: Son of Abinadab who accompanied the ark of the covenant
summary: Ahjo belonged to the family of Abinadab in Kiriath-Jearim, where the ark of the covenant had been kept for about twenty years after the Philistines returned it. As the son of Abinadab and brother of Uzza, he had a special connection to the ark and responsibility for it. When King David decided to bring the ark to Jerusalem, Ahjo went ahead of the new cart carrying it, likely to lead the ox team and clear the way for the procession. His brother Uzza walked beside the cart. During the journey, the oxen stumbled; Uzza reached out to steady the ark, and God’s anger struck him so that he died. This shocking event caused David to postpone the entire project. Ahjo’s role illustrates how one family in Israel was given a unique responsibility connected to the ark and God’s holy presence. The Hebrew name Ahjo (אַחְיוֹ) can also be understood as "his brother," and among scholars there is discussion about whether the term in 2 Sam 6 is a proper name or a designation. Another person with the same name is mentioned in Benjamin’s genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Transport of the ark of the covenant from Abinadab's house
keyEvents.description: When David attempted to bring the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem, it was placed on a new cart from Abinadab's house. Ahjo walked in front of the cart and led the procession, while his brother Uzza walked beside it.

keyEvents.title: Uzza's death at the ark of the covenant
keyEvents.description: During the transport, the oxen stumbled, and Uzza reached out his hand toward the ark to steady it. God's anger burned against Uzza, and he died there by the ark of the covenant. This event shook David and caused him to delay moving the ark.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: First Chronicles recounts the same story about transporting the ark of the covenant from Abinadab's house, where Ahjo walked in front of the cart.

versions.summary: Ahjo is a person mentioned in the Bible in connection with the genealogies in 1 Chronicles and as one of those who accompanied the ark of the covenant when it was moved. He was the son of Abinadab and served together with his brother Uzza during the transport of God's ark of the covenant.
versions.title: Benjamite mentioned in the genealogies
versions.reason: [major] The title 'Benjaminite mentioned in the genealogies' is misleading. Ahjo is primarily known as the son of Abinadab who walked before the ark of the covenant during its transport to Jerusalem. There may be two different people with the same name—one in Benjamin's genealogy and one at the ark—but the title should reflect the most prominent role.; [minor] The epoch 'united-kingdom' is reasonable if Ahjo is primarily linked to David's time and the transport of the ark. This is correct.; [major] The role 'leader' is imprecise. Ahjo was not a leader in the true sense. He walked before the ark during its transport—a more appropriate role would be 'servant at the ark' or similar. He had a serving function, not a leadership function.; [major] The summary possibly mixes two different people. The Ahjo mentioned in 1 Chron 8:14 in Benjamin's genealogy is likely another person than Ahjo who was the son of Abinadab and walked before the ark (2 Sam 6:3-4). The summary should clarify this. In addition, Ahjo is referred to as 'son of Abinadab', but this is based on the text in 2 Sam 6:3-4—the Hebrew expression can also be interpreted differently.; [minor] 1 Chron 8:14 mentions an 'Ahjo' among Benjamin's descendants, but this is likely another person than Ahjo who was with the ark. It should be clarified that this possibly is another person with the same name.; [minor] The reference 2 Sam 6:3-4 (bookId 10) is correct. BookId 10 = 2 Samuel is accurate.; [minor] That Abinadab is Ahjo's father is based on 2 Sam 6:3 where it says they drove the ark 'from Abinadab's house' and that 'Abinadab's sons' Uzza and Ahjo led the cart. Some scholars discuss whether this is the same Abinadab as in 1 Sam 7:1, but the identification is reasonable.

footnotes.text: The name Ahjo (Hebrew: אַחְיוֹ, 'Achyo') may mean "his brother" or "brotherly." Some scholars have debated whether this in 2 Sam 6:3–4 is actually a proper name or if the Hebrew expression should be translated as "his brother," that is, an anonymous brother of Uzza. Most translations, however, treat it as a proper name.

Abinadab, Ahjo's father, is likely the same person as Abinadab from Kiriath-Jearim, in whose house the ark had stood for about 20 years after it was returned by the Philistines (1 Sam 7:1–2). The family thus had a long tradition as guardians of the ark.

There are likely two different people named Ahjo in the Old Testament: one who was the son of Abinadab and participated in the transport of the ark (2 Sam 6:3–4), and another mentioned in Benjamin's genealogy (1 Chron 8:14). These should not automatically be identified as the same person.

The transport of the ark on a cart instead of carrying it with poles, as the Mosaic law prescribed (Num 4:15; Exod 25:14), has been seen as the cause of the dramatic event in which Uzza died. David later organized the transport according to the regulations of the law (1 Chron 15:13–15).

In the ancient Middle East, it was common to transport holy objects on carts, a practice widespread among the Philistines and other nations. The fact that the ark was carried on a new cart may reflect the Philistine practice when they returned the ark (1 Sam 6:7–8), rather than the Levitical arrangement prescribed in the Torah.
